phases.name: Define ranking and event semantics
phases.description: Preserve the live brief, make unknown scale targets explicit, and define event identity and ranking semantics before choosing a data path.

phases.name: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
phases.description: Use existing catalog clients and services to validate and durably accept events, publish them through an outbox, and process keyed updates.

phases.name: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
phases.description: Persist exact aggregate state, project versioned ranking indexes, serve bounded queries, and expose freshness and failure signals.

phases.name: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
phases.description: Work through deduplication, time windows, high-cardinality storage, large-K paging, concurrency, and the missing service-level targets.

steps.phase: Define ranking and event semantics
steps.title: Start from the live problem, not assumed targets
steps.content: Live problem: Top K Elements: App Store Rankings, Amazon Bestsellers. Brief: Design a system to track and display top K items (products, apps, etc.) based on various metrics in real-time. Requirements (verbatim): Track top K items by sales/downloads/ratings; Update rankings in real-time or near real-time; Support different time windows (daily, weekly, monthly); Handle millions of items; Support multiple ranking categories; Efficient query for top K items; Handle high update volume. Constraints (verbatim): Fast ranking updates; Memory efficient for large K; Handle concurrent updates; Support time-based rankings; Accurate counting at scale. Hints supplied: Min-heap or max-heap for top K; Redis sorted sets for rankings; Periodic batch updates vs real-time; Count-min sketch for approximation; Separate computation for different windows. The brief supplies no event rate, category cardinality, K limit, latency SLO, freshness target, availability, retention, or exact window-boundary convention. Agree those before sizing or promising performance.

steps.phase: Define ranking and event semantics
steps.title: Keep capacity estimates conditional
steps.content: Millions of items and high update volume are qualitative signals, not a workload model. Measure events per second and burst shape, distinct items per category and window, number of simultaneously queried windows, K distribution, late-event rate, retention, and read/write ratio. Use those measurements to choose partition count, broker retention, aggregate-store capacity, and ranking-index memory. Do not turn the phrase high volume into an invented request rate or latency guarantee.

steps.phase: Define ranking and event semantics
steps.title: Define a versioned ranking event
steps.content: Use a stable event_id, source, category_id, item_id, metric, occurred_at, schema_version, and correction or source sequence where available. Repeated delivery of one event_id must not increment a count twice. Sales and downloads can be additive events; ratings need a defined update model, such as rating_id plus version and replacement/compensation semantics, with score_sum and rating_count retained so averages are correct. Reject or quarantine malformed, unknown-metric, and unauthorized category events instead of silently changing rankings.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Represent the business event producers
steps.content: Reuse the catalog Backend Server for the upstream product, download, and rating services. Producers emit the same stable event identity on retry and include the category, item, metric, and event time; they do not compute or publish a top-K result themselves.

component.label: Product, Download & Rating Services
component.description: Upstream systems emitting versioned business events

properties.purpose: Emit validated sales, download, and rating-change events with stable event_id, category_id, item_id, metric, occurred_at, and schema_version; retry with the same event identity.

component.highlightReason: The existing Backend Server represents the upstream business services; no new producer component type is needed.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Add the ranking client
steps.content: Use the existing Web App for category and metric selection, K, time window, and paginated results. Display the ranking's as-of time and freshness state so a lagging materialized view is not presented as current without qualification.

component.label: Rankings Client
component.description: Category, metric, window, and paginated top-K views

properties.purpose: Let users select category, sales/download/rating metric, daily/weekly/monthly window, and K; page large result sets and display the result as-of time and freshness status.

component.highlightReason: The existing Web App covers the user-facing ranking experience with no problem-specific UI node.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Add a validated API boundary
steps.content: Reuse API Gateway for authenticated producer writes and ranking reads. Validate category, metric, event shape, K bounds, and window choice; apply tenant/source policy and admission limits. Keep detailed event processing and top-K merging in backend services.

component.label: Ranking API Gateway

properties.purpose: Authenticate callers, validate event and ranking-query shapes, constrain category/metric/window/K inputs, enforce source authorization and admission limits, and route writes and reads to separate services.

component.highlightReason: The existing API Gateway exposes the needed validation, authentication, TLS, and rate-limit properties.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Separate event intake from ranking reads
steps.content: The ingestion service validates source permissions and event semantics, enforces idempotency, and commits each accepted event with an outbox record before acknowledging durable acceptance. It must not synchronously update every ranking index or wait for a full window recomputation.

component.label: Ranking Event Ingestion
component.description: Validation, idempotency, and atomic event/outbox acceptance

properties.purpose: Authorize producer identity, validate versioned metric events, deduplicate by stable event_id, and atomically persist the accepted event and outbox row before returning success; keep ranking aggregation asynchronous.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Backend Server represents ingestion logic; its durable boundary is modeled separately.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Persist accepted events and an outbox
steps.content: Reuse Database for an idempotency ledger and transactional outbox. A unique event identity and accepted payload are committed atomically; the outbox relay can safely retry after a crash. Partition and expire raw-event/deduplication records only after the agreed correction and replay horizon. The brief does not specify that horizon or a database vendor.

component.label: Accepted Event Ledger & Outbox
component.description: Unique event identities and atomic publish intent

properties.purpose: Atomically retain accepted event identities/payloads and outbox publish intent; enforce uniqueness on event_id, partition by an agreed access pattern, and retain dedupe data through the correction and replay horizon.

component.highlightReason: The existing Database supports the durable uniqueness and outbox boundary required to avoid lost or double-counted accepted events.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Relay committed events without losing retries
steps.content: Use the catalog Processing Worker to claim outbox rows, publish versioned event envelopes, and mark a row delivered only after broker acknowledgement. A crash between publish and marking may redeliver; downstream event_id deduplication makes that safe.

component.label: Event Outbox Relay
component.description: Retryable publication of durably accepted ranking events

properties.purpose: Claim committed outbox rows, publish stable versioned event envelopes, retry with bounded backoff, and mark delivery only after broker acknowledgement; tolerate duplicate publication after a crash.

component.highlightReason: The existing Processing Worker fits the retryable outbox relay role.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Buffer and partition ranking events
steps.content: Reuse Message Broker as the durable event stream. Partition by a stable category/item key so events for one ranking item are serialized in broker partition order while unrelated items process concurrently. Treat this only as processing order: count each distinct additive event once, and use source versions or explicit correction semantics for mutable updates. Retention must cover the agreed replay/recovery horizon; partition counts and retention depend on measured traffic and item skew.

component.label: Durable Ranking Event Stream

properties.purpose: Buffer versioned events durably, partition by stable category_id and item_id for per-item order and parallelism, retain through the agreed replay horizon, and expose consumer lag.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Message Broker supplies the durable asynchronous boundary without introducing a new event-bus node.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Aggregate exact event-time metrics
steps.content: Use the existing stateful Stream Processor to deduplicate replayed event IDs, apply ordered corrections, and update per-item metric state for the configured windows. Keep exact counts/sums as the authoritative path; any approximate sketch is an explicitly labeled optional estimate, never a silent replacement for accurate counts.

component.label: Windowed Ranking Aggregator
component.description: Keyed exact counts, rating aggregates, and late-event handling

properties.purpose: Deduplicate event_id, process category/item keys in order, maintain exact sales/download counts and rating score_sum/rating_count, apply correction events, and update event-time window state with a declared late-event policy.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Stream Processor explicitly supports stateful and windowed real-time processing.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Keep exact aggregates as recoverable state
steps.content: Reuse Database for exact per-category, per-item, per-metric, per-window state, rating sum/count, source versions, and committed aggregate revisions. Use atomic conditional updates and a durable change outbox so retries cannot apply an increment twice and downstream index updates can resume.

component.label: Exact Aggregate State
component.description: Partitioned counts, rating sums, window state, and change outbox

properties.purpose: Persist exact aggregate values keyed by category, item, metric, and time window; store rating score_sum and rating_count, enforce idempotent versioned updates, and atomically record ranking-index change intent for recovery.

component.highlightReason: A durable aggregate store keeps exact counts independent of the derived cache and supports repair after projection loss.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Project committed rank changes
steps.content: A separate worker consumes durable aggregate-change intent and updates the Redis read index using monotonic aggregate revisions. If it falls behind or crashes, it resumes from the durable cursor; the index is rebuildable from exact aggregate state rather than treated as the source of truth.

component.label: Ranking Index Projector
component.description: Idempotent, versioned projection into sorted-set indexes

properties.purpose: Read durable aggregate change records, idempotently upsert item scores into Redis sorted sets using monotonic revisions, checkpoint only after successful projection, and rebuild indexes from exact aggregate state.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Processing Worker separates durable aggregate commits from a recoverable low-latency read projection.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Add sharded ranking indexes
steps.content: Use the catalog Cache for Redis sorted sets keyed by category, metric, window, and rank shard. Keep exact scores for each indexed item and version each update; shard to bound per-key load and memory. Redis is a derived index, so cache loss triggers rebuild or an exact-store fallback, not data loss.

component.label: Redis Ranking Indexes
component.description: Versioned sorted sets partitioned by category, metric, window, and shard

properties.purpose: Maintain versioned exact item scores in sorted sets keyed by category, metric, time window, and rank shard; bound shard memory, page large K reads, and rebuild from the durable aggregate store after loss.

component.highlightReason: The existing Cache catalog component supports Redis and cluster mode; sorted sets provide efficient score-ordered reads.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Serve bounded, deterministic top-K reads
steps.content: Use a separate query service to validate K and filters, read the requested category/metric/window from sorted-set shards, merge candidates using score plus a stable item-ID tie-breaker, and return an as-of revision. For a cache miss or stale shard, use the exact aggregate index or report partial/stale state; do not silently return an incomplete ranking as complete.

component.label: Top-K Query Service
component.description: Shard fan-out, deterministic merge, and bounded pagination

properties.purpose: Validate K and category/metric/window, query rank shards, merge exact candidates by score and stable item_id, paginate large K responses, return as-of revision/freshness, and fall back or flag incomplete cache state.

component.highlightReason: The catalog Backend Server keeps ranking reads separate from high-volume event intake.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Observe freshness and correctness
steps.content: Monitor accepted/rejected and duplicate events, outbox age, broker lag, late-event corrections, aggregate commit failures, projector lag, index rebuild progress, query latency, and result freshness. Set alert thresholds only after product and operations define objectives.

component.label: Ranking Pipeline Monitoring
component.description: Freshness, correctness, lag, saturation, and alerts

properties.purpose: Measure event acceptance and duplicates, outbox age, broker and projector lag, correction rate, exact aggregate conflicts, cache rebuild progress, query performance, and ranking as-of freshness; alert against agreed targets.

component.highlightReason: The existing Monitoring catalog component exposes metrics and alerting for the update and query paths.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Submit producer events over the authenticated API
steps.content: Business services send versioned events over TLS with a stable idempotency identity. A retry reuses the same event_id; a genuinely new sale, download, or rating change gets a new identity.

connection.label: Versioned metric events
connection.description: Authenticated event submissions with stable identity, category, item, metric, and event time.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Send ranking queries through the same boundary
steps.content: The client requests category, metric, window, K, and a continuation cursor. Input validation and access policy happen before shard fan-out.

connection.label: Top-K query and page cursor
connection.description: Validated category, metric, time-window, K, and continuation requests.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Route event writes to ingestion
steps.content: Keep the write route separate from reads so an update burst can be admitted and buffered without starving ranking queries. Return success only after the event/outbox transaction is durable.

connection.label: Validated event intake
connection.description: Authorized, bounded writes routed to the idempotent ingestion service.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Commit event identity and publish intent atomically
steps.content: A uniqueness conflict for an already accepted event_id returns the prior acceptance result without applying another increment. Store accepted data and outbox intent in one transaction to close the database/broker dual-write gap.

connection.label: Idempotent event and outbox commit
connection.description: Unique event record and durable publish intent committed together.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Make the outbox recoverable
steps.content: The relay polls or claims committed outbox rows with a lease, publishes them, and advances its cursor only after acknowledgement. A crash can cause duplicate delivery, which downstream deduplication handles.

connection.label: Committed outbox records
connection.description: Leased durable events replayable after relay or broker interruption.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Publish into the durable stream
steps.content: Partition messages by category_id and item_id, carry event_id and schema version, and retain enough history to replay the agreed recovery window. Monitor producer backpressure rather than dropping accepted events.

connection.label: Partitioned ranking events
connection.description: Replayable event envelopes keyed by category and item for per-item ordering.

steps.phase: Build durable ingestion and exact aggregation
steps.title: Consume and checkpoint keyed updates
steps.content: The stream processor replays from committed offsets, deduplicates by event identity, and checkpoints state with progress. Keyed partitioning serializes processing for one item in broker-arrival order, but it does not establish which concurrent mutable source update is authoritative; compare source sequence or revision, or apply explicit correction semantics, before committing. Preserve every distinct additive event through idempotency instead of dropping it as stale. Unrelated keys remain parallel.

connection.label: Ordered keyed event stream
connection.description: Durable replay and partition checkpoints for exact keyed aggregation.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Commit exact aggregate revisions
steps.content: Use atomic idempotent aggregate writes with a stable event/revision identity. Keep corrections explicit and recompute affected item/window scores; do not let a late duplicate silently inflate the rank.

connection.label: Exact versioned window aggregates
connection.description: Idempotent counts, rating sums/counts, corrections, and durable projection intent.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Project from committed state, not transient memory
steps.content: The projector reads durable aggregate-change records and uses monotonic revisions. It can retry or rebuild after downtime without losing the authoritative count or applying stale scores over newer ones.

connection.label: Committed aggregate change feed
connection.description: Resumable revisions for rebuilding derived category/window ranking indexes.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Maintain sorted-set projections idempotently
steps.content: Update an item score only when the incoming aggregate revision is newer. Index keys include category, metric, window, and shard; the projection exposes its applied revision so query code can judge freshness.

connection.label: Versioned Redis score upserts
connection.description: Idempotent item-score materialization for sorted-set top-K access.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Route reads to a dedicated query service
steps.content: Keep query fan-out, pagination, and merging isolated from event ingestion. Enforce agreed maximum K and response-size limits at the API boundary.

connection.label: Validated ranking read
connection.description: Bounded category, metric, window, K, and cursor request.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Fetch and merge shard candidates
steps.content: Each shard returns enough candidates to prove the global first K under the exact-score and deterministic item-ID ordering, such as up to K candidates per shard followed by cursor-based refill when needed. Because each item has one stable shard owner, candidates do not double-count across shards. Use cursors for large K rather than allocating or transferring an unbounded result.

connection.label: Shard top-K reads
connection.description: Bounded sorted-set page reads with stable ownership and revision metadata.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Keep an exact fallback and repair path
steps.content: When cache state is missing, stale, or rebuilding, query the exact aggregate index within the same bounded-response contract or return a clearly marked stale/partial result. Never treat approximate sketches as exact results.

connection.label: Exact fallback and reconciliation
connection.description: Authoritative scores and revisions for cache misses, repair, and correctness checks.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Measure API admission and query behavior
steps.content: Track rejected events and requests, per-source throttling, query latency by K/category/window, response size, and errors without logging sensitive payloads.

connection.label: API traffic and admission metrics
connection.description: Rate-limit decisions, validation outcomes, request latency, and errors.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Alert on durable backlog
steps.content: Monitor broker availability, partition skew, producer backpressure, retention headroom, and consumer lag. A growing lag means the system is not meeting the agreed freshness target even if every event remains durable.

connection.label: Durability, skew, and consumer lag
connection.description: Signals for event backlog, replay capacity, and partition imbalance.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Watch exact aggregation health
steps.content: Observe checkpoint age, duplicate suppression, correction rate, late-event watermarks, per-key skew, state size, and failed transactions. These distinguish correct-but-lagging output from dropped or double-applied events.

connection.label: Checkpoint, correction, and window metrics
connection.description: Correctness and processing-health evidence for stateful event aggregation.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Reconcile aggregate commits
steps.content: Compare committed event offsets and aggregate revisions; alert on stuck outbox rows, conditional-write conflicts, reconciliation drift, and storage headroom. Retain a repair/replay procedure with an auditable correction record.

connection.label: Aggregate and outbox correctness
connection.description: Durable revisions, reconciliation drift, write conflicts, and recovery signals.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Bound and rebuild ranking-index memory
steps.content: Measure memory per category/metric/window/shard, key cardinality, eviction, index revision lag, and rebuild duration. Prefer bounded pages and deliberate sharding; evicting authoritative rank members without a fallback can return incorrect top-K results, so treat such eviction as a degraded state.

connection.label: Index memory, revision, and rebuild metrics
connection.description: Signals for memory efficiency, staleness, and cache recovery.

steps.phase: Materialize and serve top-K rankings
steps.title: Expose accepted-event and outbox health
steps.content: Track dedupe hits, invalid events, transaction retries, outbox age, and acceptance latency. An API success means durable acceptance, not that the new event is already visible in every ranking window.

connection.label: Accepted event and outbox metrics
connection.description: Durable-acceptance latency, validation, deduplication, and retry signals.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Make exactness the default contract
steps.content: For sales/download totals, apply each accepted event once. For ratings, define whether a rating is an immutable event or a mutable entity; if mutable, use rating_id and versioned replacement/compensation so score_sum and rating_count reflect the latest accepted value. A count-min sketch can be an optional explicitly approximate discovery mode, but it cannot satisfy an exact ranking response by itself.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Define window boundaries and late data
steps.content: Daily, weekly, and monthly can mean calendar periods or rolling durations; the brief does not decide. Pick a timezone and boundary convention, retain event time, and use watermarks plus a documented correction horizon. Apply a late event to affected windows and publish a new aggregate revision; outside the correction horizon, reconcile explicitly rather than silently ignoring it.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Scale without splitting one item's ordering
steps.content: Assign each category/item to one stable rank shard so concurrent updates for that item are serialized and its score is not duplicated across shards. Query each shard for bounded candidates and merge globally. Measure hot-key skew; if one item dominates, introduce a documented partial-counter scheme whose exact merge and correction behavior is tested before routing that key differently.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Keep large-K reads memory bounded
steps.content: Do not materialize every matching item in one application response. Enforce a product-approved K ceiling or serve stable cursor pages; bound shard fan-out and page size, and use a deterministic score/item-ID order so ties do not repeat or disappear between pages. The maximum K and response budget are not specified by the live problem.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Isolate category and metric namespaces
steps.content: Include category, metric, window, and shard in aggregate and index keys. Validate category membership and metric compatibility before accepting events; never let one category's score leak into another. Keep metric definitions versioned because a sales count, download count, and average rating have different aggregation and correction rules.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Turn near-real-time into a measurable objective
steps.content: The write path is durably accepted before asynchronous aggregation and index projection finish. Return as-of revision/time and measure event-to-visible-ranking lag. Agree a freshness percentile and query-latency objective with users and operators, then alert on broker, aggregate, and projector lag against it; the brief supplies no numeric SLO.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Recover from duplicates, crashes, and cache loss
steps.content: Test producer retry, relay crash after publish, duplicate broker delivery, processor restart, concurrent same-item updates, late corrections, database retry, and Redis loss. Durable IDs, ordered partition offsets, atomic aggregate revisions, and a replayable index projection should preserve exact totals. Rebuild derived sorted sets from the exact store and report freshness during recovery.

steps.phase: Review correctness, scale, and operational limits
steps.title: Review the design and resolve open targets
steps.content: The graph now has a durable event path, exact windowed aggregates, rebuildable ranking indexes, bounded top-K reads, and observable freshness. Before production sizing, decide event and item cardinality, update bursts, K limits, metric/rating correction rules, window timezone, replay/correction retention, freshness and query SLOs, availability, and budget. Validate shard memory and hot-key behavior from measured workloads rather than treating this review draft as a capacity guarantee.
